renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Ageless he stands, deathless, dressed in atom-small powers — dear to the yoginis, lord who gathers all. Freed while living, acting yet never stained — this body, if you see it right, is the great lord's own supreme body, O god.

Who falls silent here, who sits, who worships? Who gets pleased, O great lord — ask it and watch the questions answer themselves. Whose fire-gift, whose offering, how, and what? All that working is outer work, done in coarse things only.

The real saying-over is this: in the highest state, what ponders is pondering itself — muttering there, self-sound, mantra-natured, just so. Sitting is a still mind with no shape and no prop — not sitting is picturing bodies, eyes, mouths, hands.

Worship named is not flowers — it is mind made steady, melting out of caring into the sky-with-no-seams. Stand in the one-yoking, day after day — the full-formed state ripens: content here, full to the brim.

In the great open-abode, in fire, lay sense-things and the rest — offered by mind, the whole gift, with knowing for a spoon. The offering here, highest lady, is being content, bliss-marked — it wears sins away and shelters all: the mountain's daughter.

Who goes mute, who sits, who worships — who gets pleased, great lord? The questions file themselves. Whose fire-gift, whose sacrifice, what, how? Outer ops in coarse stuff only.

Actual recitation: top state edition — contemplation contemplating itself, muttering as self-sound, mantra-built, like that. Meditation is motionless mind, formless, propless — not-meditation is staging bodies, eyes, mouths, hands.
